findings.description: The 'data' bucket is created with no ACL restriction, no public access block, and no bucket policy restricting access; the inline comment confirms the bucket is intended to be public. It also holds a customer master file, so sensitive data would be world-readable.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects including customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE/KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so access to a bucket containing customer data leaves no audit trail, hampering detection of unauthorised access.
Versioning is disabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed irrecoverably by an attacker or accidental apply.
A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded to the unencrypted, publicly accessible 'data' bucket and no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption is specified on the object itself.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose financial data publicly; defence in depth is absent.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial records, so there is no audit trail of object access.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, allowing irreversible deletion or overwrite of financial objects.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operations data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, so object-level access to this bucket is not recorded for audit or incident response.
The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, relying solely on the private ACL and leaving no guardrail against future public exposure.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so datasets are stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource guards this bucket, so account-level or later ACL/policy changes could make its contents public.
The log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no policy enforcing TLS (aws:SecureTransport); log data could be exposed or transmitted in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The central log bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or exfiltration of audit logs would go unrecorded.
